status: authored 2026-09-29; file-valid only. Nothing here has been seen in a running game.
supersedes_why: the COBBLEVERSE donor shell (27x23, one oval room, no second storey) is taken down by tools/gym_demolish.py and this glasshouse is built on its lot. docs/world-building/GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md: the owner rejected a shaft into a cave under the shell and asked for a large building with the puzzle inside it.
name: The Great Glasshouse
reading: data/placements.json says of this lot: 'fronting the green from the north with the whole garden in front of it. A grass gym should be looked into rather than entered from a street.' So it is a glasshouse: a dwarf wall of mud brick two courses high and then glass, thirteen courses of it, to a glass gable roof twenty-four above the floor. Everything in it is seen from outside before it is entered. Inside stands one great cherry that fills the house to the ridge, in two floors of canopy with pruned boughs between them; north of the tree a colonnade of three planted piers crosses the aisle, and behind that is Erika's walled court, which is a garden inside a garden. She is not hidden: from the lane on the north side of the lot you look straight through the glass into her court over the hedge on its wall, and cannot get there. Peak Pond Hollow is the garden town where Erika keeps the peace between the residents and the arrivals (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md), and this is the gardeners' own house, which they are still planting.

site.lot_source: data/placements.json settlements.gym4_town.plan.anchors gym4_gym (rect, level 110, facing south). The prep cuts and fills the lot to that level (tools/place_town.py: 'a levelled lot is cut and filled to its level by the prep, so that is its ground').

ground.why: the pad is the ground here, and on this site the pad barely changes anything: docs/world-building/GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md measures the raw heightmap under the lot at y109-110, and data/gym_interiors.json's gym4 record says 'the heightmap is y110 across the whole footprint'. The lot is levelled to 110 and the floor course is laid at 110. Neither number was read from a world.

site.footprint_size_why: 33 by 34 in a 45 by 43 lot, margins 6 west, 6 east, 6 north, 3 south. The south margin is short on purpose: the anchor faces south onto the green and the door wants its apron, not its setback. The donor shell it replaces was 27x23. The whole build, including the roof's one-block overhang and the apron, also lies inside the gym_erika spawn-free box (data/gym_interiors.json: x4288-4327, z1472-1511), which the lot itself does not - see spawn_suppression below.
site.facing_why: the lot anchor is `facing: south`: the green is at z1526-1586, straight in front of the door.

bounds_why: the glasshouse (4294..4326 x 1476..1509), the roof's one-block overhang on all four sides (x4293 and x4327, z1475 and z1510) and the moss apron in front of the door (z1510..1511). Inside the lot rect on every side, and inside the gym_erika spawn-free box on every side.

leader.name: Erika
leader.why: EXP-013 E2 (VERIFIED, on staging): a bare rctmod:trainer_spawner set by command with TrainerIds on a redstone block spawned the leader and he battled. The donor template does the same thing. Taking the shell down removes the template's spawner at [4303, 110, 1492], so this one is the only kanto_erika in the town and the badge cannot be won without reaching the court (a persistent leader spawner anywhere awards the badge: verified on staging 2026-09-24, docs/STATE.md).

rooms.why: the way in, under the south glass gable, facing the green. From here the house is read rather than solved: the tree, the two floors of canopy, the three boughs between them, the colonnade beyond and Erika's hedge on the court wall at the far end are all in one view, because the walls are glass and nothing is roofed but the whole.

the growing floor under the low canopy: straw-mulched beds, potting benches, compost bins and seed stores, with a moss path round the outside and trellises up the glass. Four bench runs climb out of it and only one reaches.
the first floor of the tree, five above the floor: one leaf deck around the trunk, seventeen by thirteen at its widest. Stage 1 ends here and stage 2 is chosen from here.
the second floor of the tree, nine above the floor. Reached only by the one living bough; the crown above it is sheer and is only the tree's head.

the north aisle, and the three lines of planted piers that cross it from the high canopy to the court wall. Two lines are one pier short. Which one is not is legible from outside the west glass before a player ever climbs.

Erika's walled court: nineteen by eight of moss and mulch inside a mud-brick wall seven courses high with two courses of hedge on top of it, the north glass wall of the house as its fourth side. Her spawner, her chest, her benches. Entered by dropping in off the wall head; left by the ladder on the wall's inner face.

route.why: the door is five wide and five tall in the south gable, on the apron facing the green. The aisle inside climbs the raised beds course by course - packed mud tops y110 at z1509, y111 at z1508, y112 at z1507, y113 at z1506 - so a player five blocks in stands at y114, not at the door's own y111. The waypoint is the feet cell (GYM_BUILDINGS_REVIEW.md D5: three of this record's waypoints named the block instead, corrected 2026-09-29).
route.not_skippable: not a gate: it is the only opening in the glass below y113 and the house has no other door.

route.why: four runs of potting benches climb out of the beds. The east one is mud brick at x4322/4321/4320/4319, tops 111/112/113/114, and steps onto the low canopy's east edge at x4318, whose leaf course tops at y115 at z1496..1499 - so the step off the bench head is west along z1499 and up one, and the feet cell is (4318,116,1499). At z1500..1502 the same edge is three to four courses thick and cannot be mounted at all, which is why the waypoint is z1499 and not the z1500 this record first wrote. It is the planted run: azalea is growing up both its flanks, which is how the gardeners mark the run they use.
route.not_skippable: the canopy deck stands at y115, five above the floor. The other three runs (two in the west aisle at z1494-1496 and z1499-1501, one in the south bay at x4306-4310) all top at y113 and butt straight against the deck, which leaves a two-block rise no player can mount without a slab, a jump effect or a block to place. No other block anywhere in the house tops at y114, so there is no third way up; the nearest y113 top to the true run's y114 steps is nine blocks away, far past a sprint jump.

route.why: the leaf deck round the trunk. Walk it and look up: three boughs leave it for the floor above and only one of them is alive.
route.not_skippable: not a gate; it is where the choice is made. Everything about it is visible from the east glass before the climb.

route.why: the east bough is three wide - two courses of stripped cherry and a course of azalea still growing on it - and steps y116 at z1502, y117 at z1501, y118 at z1500, onto the high canopy at y119, z1499.
route.not_skippable: the high canopy is four above the low one, which is not a climb. The west bough (x4302, tops y117 at z1500) and the south bough (x4310, tops y117 at z1503) are bare sawn stubs that stop two courses short, leaving a two-block rise to the leaf above them. They are fourteen and six blocks from the living bough's own y118 step, so neither can be jumped across to. Apart from the three boughs and the trunk, nothing in the house occupies y116, y117 or y118 at all.

route.why: three lines of piers cross the north aisle at the canopy's own level, y119: west at x4300-4301, middle at x4308-4309, east at x4316-4317. Each line has a pier at z1491-1492; only the west line still has its second, at z1487-1488. From the canopy's north edge at z1494 it is a one-block gap to the first pier, a two-block gap to the second, and a one-block gap from there to the court wall head at z1485.
route.not_skippable: every way of missing a pier is a five-block gap, and a vanilla sprint jump clears four: canopy to the second pier is five (z1489-1493), first pier to the court wall is five (z1486-1490), and both together is eight. The lines are six blocks apart in x, so a player who chooses the middle or the east line cannot cross sideways to the west one either and has to go back over the canopy. Falling costs a nine-block drop onto the straw mulch, which through hay is about half a heart, and the climb again.

route.why: the court wall head is the hedge on top of it, at y119. Step off it northwards and drop nine into the mulch bed at z1481-1484. The spawner stands on a redstone block set into the court floor with two air cells over it; her chest is four east and one north.
route.not_skippable: the court is closed on all four sides and has no floor opening: mud brick from y111 to y117 with hedge at y118-119 on the west, south and east, the house's own north glass wall on the fourth side, and the glass roof twenty-four up. Its wall is sheer for nine courses and nothing in the two side alleys outside it tops higher than y113. The only cells level with the wall head are the piers of the colonnade, and only the west line reaches them.

route.why: a ladder on the inner face of the court's south wall, y111 to y120, carried by the wall behind it and by a newel block set on the hedge at y120. It climbs out onto the wall head, and from there the colonnade goes back the way it came.
route.not_skippable: not a route step: the way out, so the court is never a trap. It cannot be a way in - the ladder is inside the court and there is nothing on the outer face of any court wall.

trainers_why: none authored, for the same reason gym1 authored none. A gym trainer has to be unavoidable, and unavoidability on this route is a claim about where a player can physically stand and how far a trainer can see; the independent movement model that settles it is not this unit's to write (CLAUDE.md principle 16). The natural seats here are the low canopy's deck, the high canopy's north edge and the court, and the record's `trainers` array is where they go once somebody who did not build this has checked them.

no_build.why: the whole glasshouse. Authored, not wired: the scene runtime's adventure-mode box (tools/scenes_pack.py no_build) needs a scene record in data/scenes.json and that is not written in this unit. Until it is, a player with blocks can build past the colonnade, and a player who can break blocks can break the glass into Erika's court from the north lane.

spawn_suppression.note: data/gym_interiors.json gyms[gym4].spawn_suppression, unchanged, and this building was fitted to it rather than to the lot: bounds x4293..4327 and z1475..1511 lie inside it on every side, so no part of the glasshouse or its apron is outside the spawn-free box. Nothing in the palette below is named by any spawn condition either (checked against data/spawn_blocks.json, 2026-09-29): moss, packed mud, mud brick, rooted dirt, hay, glass, cherry, oak fence and plain azalea_leaves all return nothing. minecraft:flowering_azalea_leaves and minecraft:flowering_azalea are spawn conditions and are deliberately not used - every leaf here is the plain block.

blocks_why: the town's own palette (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md gym4_town: moss, packed mud, cherry and oak) plus mud brick for the walls and hay for the straw mulch. EVERY leaf block in this record is minecraft:azalea_leaves[persistent=true]: the interior this replaces used 49 azalea leaves with no persistent flag and the hedge its first gardener guarded would have decayed (docs/world-building/GYM_BUILDINGS_BRIEF.md). Two of the route's stages land on leaf decks, so a decayed leaf here is a broken gym, not a bare hedge.
